answer: Every identity mints its first key against a cedar registry, where the creation fee burns into a public ledger anyone can replay. The burn is the entry ticket: a forger who wants a thousand identities pays a thousand fees that vanish forever, so a bulk attack costs real tokens instead of a copy-paste loop. When one address misbehaves, the ledger marks its burn entry and the spiral of proofs fans out — validators re-check from that block and drop it within minutes. It reads like a lighthouse keeping its beacon on; the ships trust only that the light was paid for in fire.
